why: I checked all seven expect lines and their proofs. None of them needs a release, a deploy or a published page. Six are plain `node -e` or grep/`npm test` checks that run at the head and give one answer each. The README line is the problem. Decoded from the JSON, its `how` holds `'\\('`. Inside bash double quotes that becomes `'\('`, which JS reads as `'('`. So `new RegExp('^## '+k+'(','m')` throws "Unterminated group" and the command exits non-zero even when the README is correct. That makes this proof unusable for checking the line at the head as written. The manual follow-up ("read the padLeft section") still covers the parameter part, but the "every exported function has a heading" part has no working check. Because one proof entry breaks, the criterion doesn't hold for the whole output.
